newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, North Korea plan new bilateral accord.
newsitem.headline: Russia, North Korea plan new bilateral accord.

text.p: Russia and North Korea will soon embark on discussions for a new bilateral treaty to strengthen ties that have frayed since the collapse of the Soviet Union, Itar-Tass news agency reported on Friday.

Tass quoted deputy foreign minister Grigory Karasin as saying the accord would be "an important step towards the further development of equal, mutually beneficial cooperation between both countries", but he gave no further details.

"The most important thing is not to allow an escalation of tension in the region and to renew the inter-Korean peace process," Karasin said, adding that Russia had a strong interest in promoting stability on her Far Eastern borders.

But he cast doubts on the usefulness of a U.S. proposal for talks involving North and South Korea, China and the United States. He suggested a wider forum, including Russia, Japan and the United Nations, should be convened.

Pyongyang's relations with Moscow have cooled since the demise of the Soviet Union but Russia remains a favoured partner in many spheres. On Friday Russia dispatched a new ambassador, Valery Denisov, to Pyongyang, Tass said.
